text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.2% today as oil prices climbed following U.S. military strikes against Iranian targets, with Brent crude jumping above $90 a barrel. Refineries are running near full capacity at 97.4%, and the company benefits directly when crude prices rise — higher oil prices typically improve refinery margins (the difference between what they pay for crude and what they can sell refined products for), even as global crude inventories remain elevated at 718.6 million barrels.

The stock's gains over the past two weeks (4.2%) also reflect the broader support refiners are getting from geopolitical tension. Meanwhile, the White House is meeting with U.S. oil refiners this week about boosting capacity, which signals potential tailwinds for the sector — though the announced Venezuela oil deal and near-term output increases could eventually pressure prices if they materialize, offsetting some of these near-term gains.
